use_when: a bounded specialist-agent role is genuinely missing after checking the host's native agents, existing project agents, Skills, and local procedures
project-aware curation of specialist role prompts would materially improve specialization or context isolation
avoid_when: the main agent can perform the work adequately
the need is actually a technical tool or external-service capability gap rather than a role/specialization gap
installing a broad catalog would add context or coordination overhead without a concrete responsibility boundary
the task is blocked by authorization, credentials, environment, network, external dependency, or product decision

notes: On Windows use bootstrap.ps1 instead of bootstrap.sh.

Provider detection is intentionally empty because the current installer does not create a provider-specific ownership marker. Generic files under .claude/agents, .cursor/agents, or similar directories are not proof that agent-bundles was installed.
Preview with --dry-run before installation and prefer one or a few explicit divisions that match the evidenced responsibility gap; do not use the broad project/default bundle merely for convenience.

Record the agent-bundles revision and the resolved upstream agency-agents revision when the specialist prompts become material to a project, because the upstream is fetched at runtime and can change independently.
Review the selected role files as procedural input before relying on them in a sensitive project; upstream role prompts are installed as-is rather than vendored or independently certified by AAOP.
agent-bundles does not vendor upstream agents. Its bootstrap fetches msitarzewski/agency-agents at runtime and installs a curated subset into the selected host's agent directory.

permissions: local write access to the selected host's agent configuration directory
network access to GitHub for the agent-bundles repository and its configured upstream source

checks: confirm only the intended specialist divisions/agents were installed
confirm generic pre-existing agent files were not mistaken for agent-bundles ownership
record or inspect the concrete provider/upstream revisions used for material adoption
restart or reload the host if it requires agent discovery at startup
delegate one bounded representative responsibility and verify that specialist separation materially improves the original task
remove or avoid specialists that duplicate the main agent without measurable value

steps: remove only the agent files proven to have been installed for this adoption from the target host agent directory
preserve project-owned or pre-existing agent files
remove the temporary agent-bundles checkout if it is no longer needed

warnings: Agent-role prompts do not create new external tool permissions or technical capabilities; do not misclassify a missing tool/API/runtime as something more agents can solve.
More agents can increase coordination cost and context fragmentation. Default to one agent unless the responsibility boundary is evidenced.
The current agent-bundles installer has no provider-specific ownership marker, so AAOP must not infer installation merely from the presence of generic host agent files.
Runtime-fetched upstream role prompts can change; consequential reuse should capture the actual revisions and review the selected files rather than assuming a prior catalog review still applies.
